original_test_intent: Validate the GB PCIe switch temperature sensor across complete IB/OOB SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web evidence against the approved PEX thermal specification.
original_method: The platform owner binds TEMP_GB_PEX_SW to the exact switch ASIC and board location, defines whether it measures junction, remote diode or board temperature, supplies traffic/airflow-qualified limits, and automation passively collects evidence.
manual_activity: The PCIe/thermal owner maps the exact GB switch and sensing point, approves operating-state limits, then reviews the complete management and passive link-health evidence.
required_inputs: GB board revision and exact PCIe switch vendor/device/instance and physical coordinate
Stable identity such as serial, device path, fabric role and PCI BDF where applicable
TEMP_GB_PEX_SW sensing source: switch junction, internal/remote diode or board probe
Units, scale, tolerance, refresh, stale/unavailable and threshold/hysteresis semantics
Normal and limit ranges by negotiated link state, passive traffic level, airflow and ambient
SDR entity/name/description plus Sensor List/Web mapping and same-target BMC/PEX/spec revisions
Secret-safe ipmitool collection and approved passive PCIe inventory/health source
Independent PCIe, cooling, BMC and platform recovery
safety_requirements: Bind the sensor to one exact PEX device and sensing point before temperature comparison
Record passive link speed/width, error health and traffic context because switch dissipation is state dependent
Do not infer junction limits for a remote board probe or vice versa
Do not rescan PCIe, generate traffic, reload drivers, change thresholds/cooling/BMC or clear logs
Stop on device disappearance, link degradation, stale/invalid sensor, threshold event or incomplete views
agent_execution_scope: Verify unique source, exact PEX identity, sensor source and same-target mapping
Collect complete secret-safe IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List, exact sensor result and BMC Web
Collect passive PEX inventory, link width/speed/error, airflow/ambient and SEL context
Compare only to owner-approved limits for the observed state
Perform no PCIe action, workload, driver/cooling/threshold/BMC/log mutation, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the switch ASIC, board location, stable identity and fabric role
Define the thermal sensing point and state-qualified limits
Approve Web/SDR identity mapping and passive health context
Review evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES PEX ASIC IDENTITY, SENSOR-LOCATION SEMANTICS AND LINK-STATE THERMAL ENVELOPE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Join the BMC sensor to a stable PEX device/fabric identity, identify its sensing point, and compare synchronized temperature with passive link, error and cooling context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the device/sensor topology needed to interpret one generic GB PEX temperature name.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The following FPGA temperature is a separate component and provides no PEX switch coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A remote board probe can lag and read far below switch junction temperature; applying junction thresholds to it, or board-probe limits to a die sensor, makes an apparently clean reading misleading.

project_override_considerations: If multiple PEX devices exist behind this single label, the owner must define aggregation or select the exact device. Dynamic BDF alone should be paired with a stable topology identifier.
expected_evidence: Approved GB board/PEX ASIC/location/fabric identity and sensing-source map
Units, freshness, thresholds and link/traffic/airflow-qualified thermal criteria
Complete redacted IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List plus exact sensor result
BMC Web, same-target proof and passive PEX link/error/traffic/ambient/SEL context

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, DeepSeek and Criteria consistently target TEMP_GB_PEX_SW; missing device and sensor semantics are project inputs, not competing source claims.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive exact-sensor review is identifiable after the owner supplies the PEX topology, sensing point and thermal envelope.

review_improvement: Adds stable switch/fabric identity, distinguishes junction from remote-board sensing and conditions acceptance on passive link and cooling state.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCIe switch power and temperature depend on active link count, negotiated speed and traffic, while a remote board sensor responds more slowly than an on-die diode. A value cannot be judged solely by its numeric range until both the sensing point and observed fabric state are known.
